roles.title: New and aspiring Scrum Masters
roles.body: The Certified Scrum Master (CSM) credential is the most widely listed entry requirement in Scrum Master job descriptions, and no prior experience is required to earn it.

roles.title: Project Managers moving to agile delivery
roles.body: PMs transitioning from predictive delivery use the CSM to relabel and rewire their facilitation and planning skills for Scrum teams.

roles.title: Developers and QA engineers
roles.body: Team members who informally run standups and retros formalize that role with the CSM, a common first step toward lead positions.

roles.title: Product Owners and Business Analysts
roles.body: Understanding the Scrum Master accountability makes backlog collaboration smoother; many POs hold both CSM and CSPO.

roles.title: Engineering Managers and Team Leads
roles.body: Leaders of Scrum teams take the CSM to coach rather than command, and to run the events their teams depend on.

roles.title: Agile Coaches starting their track
roles.body: The CSM is the first rung of the Scrum Alliance certification ladder that continues to A-CSM and CSP-SM.

p: The Certified Scrum Master (CSM) exam is a 50-question multiple-choice test with a 60-minute limit, taken online through the Scrum Alliance platform. You need 37 correct answers (74%) to pass.
The exam unlocks only after you complete the live CSM course with a licensed trainer — self-study alone cannot lead to the credential.

The sequence is: attend the full live {days}-day CSM training, receive your exam invitation from Scrum Alliance by email, take the 50-question online exam, and accept the license agreement. Your CSM certificate and two-year Scrum Alliance membership activate immediately after passing.
The course fee of {price} includes the exam — there is no separate exam purchase for candidates in {country}.

Your course fee includes two exam attempts within 90 days of the course. The pass rate is high — the exam checks understanding of the Scrum framework as taught in class, not trick questions — and a further attempt after the included two carries a small fee set by Scrum Alliance.
There is no waiting period between your first and second attempt; most candidates who retake do so within days.

The CSM exam is fully online and unproctored in the traditional sense — you take it from home or office in {city} whenever you're ready within the 90-day window. No test centres, no scheduling constraints, no timezone gymnastics.
The 60-minute timer starts when you begin; you can complete it any time of day that suits {city} hours.
The CSM credential is valid for two years. Renewal requires 20 Scrum Education Units (SEUs) earned over the period plus a renewal fee paid to Scrum Alliance — no re-examination.

SEUs come from courses, user-group participation, volunteering and other learning activities logged in your Scrum Alliance account; many CSMs simply roll their renewal into the next certification (A-CSM) on the track.

examFaqs.q: How many questions are on the CSM exam?
examFaqs.a: The CSM exam has 50 multiple-choice questions with a 60-minute limit. You need 37 correct (74%) to earn the CSM credential.
The CSM exam checks understanding of the Scrum framework as taught in the live course — no trick questions. Attend the full CSM course, review the Scrum Guide, and the pass rate is very high.

examFaqs.q: Can I take the CSM exam without the course?
examFaqs.a: No. Scrum Alliance requires attending the full live CSM course with a licensed trainer before the exam unlocks — self-study alone cannot lead to CSM certification.

examFaqs.q: How many CSM exam attempts do I get?
examFaqs.a: Your CSM course fee includes two exam attempts within 90 days. Further attempts carry a small Scrum Alliance fee; there is no waiting period between attempts.
No. The CSM exam is taken online through the Scrum Alliance platform at any time within your 90-day window — no test centres, no proctoring appointments.

examFaqs.q: Are there prerequisites for CSM certification?
examFaqs.a: None. The CSM has no degree, experience or prior-certification requirement — attending the live CSM course is the only mandatory step before the exam.

examFaqs.q: How long is the CSM certification valid?
examFaqs.a: The CSM credential is valid for two years. Renewal requires 20 SEUs plus a Scrum Alliance renewal fee — there is no re-examination for CSM renewal.

examFaqs.q: What are SEUs and how do I earn them?
examFaqs.a: Scrum Education Units (SEUs) are the renewal currency for the CSM: courses, user-group sessions, volunteering and other learning activities logged in your Scrum Alliance account count toward the 20 needed every two years.

examFaqs.q: Is the exam fee included in CSM training?
examFaqs.a: Yes. Unlike most certifications, the CSM course fee includes the exam with two attempts and two years of Scrum Alliance membership — no separate exam purchase.

examFaqs.q: CSM vs PSM — which should I take?
examFaqs.a: The CSM (Scrum Alliance) requires a live course and renews every two years; PSM I (Scrum.org) can be taken exam-only and never expires. Choose the CSM for guided, exercise-driven learning with trainer feedback; see the comparison table on this page.

examFaqs.q: Does the CSM cover scaling frameworks like SAFe?
examFaqs.a: The CSM focuses on single-team Scrum — roles, events and artifacts. It builds the foundation that scaling frameworks assume; many CSM holders add a scaling certification later.

examFaqs.q: What happens right after I pass the CSM exam?
examFaqs.a: You accept the Scrum Alliance license agreement and your CSM certificate plus two-year membership activate immediately — most candidates hold the CSM within a week of finishing class.

examFaqs.q: What is the next certification after CSM?
examFaqs.a: The Scrum Alliance track continues from CSM to Advanced Certified ScrumMaster (A-CSM) and then Certified Scrum Professional ScrumMaster (CSP-SM); many CSM holders also add CSPO for the Product Owner view.

examFaqs.q: Will I get a certificate for attending the CSM course?
examFaqs.a: Your credential comes from Scrum Alliance after passing the CSM exam — that is the certificate employers verify, and it appears in the public Scrum Alliance directory.
